summary: @servicetitan/titan-chatbot-api ships preinstall Bun-runtime dropper that executes an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<...>.zip, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync on a sibling file math_init.js shipped inside the tarball. math_init.js is a 727,680-byte Bun-compiled CJS bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) with rotated string-array obfuscation, numeric dictionaries, and randomized identifiers (e.g. MmgoCP, etDiOOB, WV8StW). setup.mjs itself uses identifier obfuscation (`_0x` naming, string dictionaries). The advertised purpose of the package is an NSwag-generated REST chatbot API client (dist/api-client/...), which has no functional need for a bundled Bun-only executable. Fetching an alternate runtime at preinstall to execute an obfuscated bundled payload is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the code that actually runs on the installer's machine is hidden from Node-based analysis inside a Bun-compiled bundle. The package name and repository URL present as a ServiceTitan first-party scope (@servicetitan/*, github.com/servicetitan/titan-chatbot-client), giving the drop cover-story branding against ServiceTitan customers and internal build systems.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
